recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No follow-up is needed in core unless a future work group decision reopens primitive datatype representation rules beyond this narrow wording clarification.
issue_request: FHIR-5234 was a Published/Persuasive DSTU1 MnM ballot clarification asking the primitive datatype text to say that elements using primitive datatypes can have identity and extensions. The resolution accepted the wording as clearer while noting that the type still permits those features.
initial_application: The Jira comments cite SVN revision 4533. Git commit d8c3b09240e38503a709e6540aea5782e76cc4f7 is the Git mirror of build@4533 and changed source/datatypes.html from "All the primitive types have..." to "All elements using these primitive types have...", applying the semantic clarification despite the historical subject referencing #5233.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini keeps datatypes.html in current build scope through the active [type-pages] default mapping for datatypes. Later line history changed the sentence to "may have one or more" and updated punctuation, but preserved the element-based wording. Zulip and Confluence searches found no relevant discussion changing that conclusion.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit is needed because source/datatypes.html already states that all elements using primitive types may have value, internal identity, and extensions.

related_jiras.note: A later editorial commit touched the same sentence for punctuation only and did not alter the FHIR-5234 element-vs-type clarification.
